content: Imagine living in a place so high that breathing is difficult, roads are covered in snow, and there are no petrol pumps or towns for miles! Have you ever wondered how people survive in such extreme cold, living 5000 meters above sea level where the temperature drops below zero?

If you had to pack your bags to live in a freezing, high-altitude desert, what is the one most important thing you would take with you? Would you build a cement house or take a tent? Why? Think about it before moving on!

content.title: The High Altitude Desert
content.description: At 5000 meters, the air is thin and cold. The Changpa tribe moves from place to place with their sheep and goats. They don't build permanent houses. Instead, they carry a special, large, cone-shaped tent.

content: Meet the **Changpa** tribe! They live high up in the mountains of Ladakh and Changthang. Their only treasure is their goats and sheep. They live in a big cone-shaped tent called a **Rebo**, which is made from yak hair strips woven together. This keeps them warm in extreme cold.

definition: A big cone-shaped tent used by the Changpa tribe, made of woven yak hair to protect them from extreme cold winds.
A nomadic tribe living in the high-altitude regions of Ladakh, known for rearing special goats that produce Pashmina wool.

question: What is the big cone-shaped tent used by the Changpa tribe called?

content: Close your eyes and imagine sleeping in a Rebo while freezing winds blow outside. The yak hair tent is strong and warm. Why do you think the Changpa people weave yak hair instead of using cotton or plastic for their tents?

The Changpa tribe's goats are very special. They have soft hair that grows in winter to protect them from the cold. In summer, they shed this hair. This fine hair is used to weave the world-famous, incredibly warm **Pashmina shawls**! Did you know a single Pashmina shawl is as warm as six thick sweaters?
Fun Fact! It takes a weaver almost 250 hours to weave one plain Pashmina shawl. It is entirely done by hand because the wool is too delicate for machines.

Can you map out a journey? Trace Gaurav Jani's route from Mumbai to Leh, passing through Delhi and Manali. What different types of houses would you see along the way? Draw a comparison between a high-rise building in Mumbai and a Rebo in Changthang!
We just saw tents high up in the dry mountains. Now, imagine opening your bedroom window and seeing a beautiful lake instead of a road! The house isn't built on land—it's floating on water!
How can a house float on water without sinking? If you were to design a floating house, what material would you use? Wood, stone, or iron?

content.title: A Floating House
content.description: Wood is lighter than water and naturally floats. By building a boat with rooms inside, people can live comfortably on lakes.

content: In Srinagar (Jammu and Kashmir), many people live on the Dal Lake and Jhelum river. Tourists love to stay in beautifully carved wooden boats called **Houseboats**, some of which are 80 feet long! Local people often live in uncarved floating houses called **Dongas**. Some houses even have special windows that come out of the wall, known as a **Dab**.

definition: A large, beautifully carved wooden boat on water where tourists stay in Srinagar.
A traditional wooden boat on Dal Lake and Jhelum river where many local families in Srinagar live.

question: What is the special window that comes out of the wall in old houses of Srinagar called?

content: Think about the difference between a Rebo in Changthang and a Houseboat in Srinagar. Why do people build such different types of shelters? How does the climate and surroundings (geography) decide the type of house people live in?

This connects to what we learned about early humans who used caves! Every human shelter, whether it's an igloo, a tent, a stilt house in a flood zone, or a houseboat, is an adaptation to survive the local climate and use local materials.
Don't confuse a Donga with a Houseboat! While both float on water in Srinagar, Houseboats are highly decorated and mostly for tourists, whereas Dongas are simpler boats where local families live.

Create your own 'Shelter Catalog'. Make a list of 4 different extreme places (e.g., a hot desert, a snowy mountain, a rainy forest, a lake). Write down what kind of shelter you would build in each place and what materials you would use!
